A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RALI/RACT research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original RALI and RACT evaluations, reasoning analyses, component and hyperparameter ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on training without reasoning, two-dataset co-training, and RACT's numerical-score source.

M1.justification: RALI retains contrastive alignment, PCA, bucketed k-means and similarity-weighted scoring; RACT retains single-domain RL, label alignment and cross-domain SFT. The new experimental variants test these mechanisms without revising the proposed methods.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight IQA datasets, including TID2013 in cross-domain experiments. The additions reuse existing data and tasks while varying training mixtures, reasoning and score sources.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LIQE and removes NIMA, although the accompanying prose still lists NIMA. New Table A.1 compares Qwen-SFT, GRPO without reasoning and Q-Insight. The existing cross-domain comparator set and 3B Q-Insight comparison are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce GRPO training without reasoning, KonIQ-plus-SPAQ training for Q-Insight and RACT, and RACT initialized from SPAQ-trained Q-Insight using SPAQ scores. Existing Section 5.1 settings, metrics, preprocessing and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the mechanism and robustness analyses: Table A.1 tests whether reasoning contributes beyond GRPO; Table A.2 combines new two-dataset experiments with existing single/four-dataset results; Table A.3 tests sensitivity to the numerical-score source. Earlier ablations and qualitative cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation repetition counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Using multiple seeds to generate training descriptions was already documented in v1 and remains unchanged.

E6.justification: New Tables A.1-A.3 substantially expand the reported findings. Table A.1 reports average PLCC/SRCC of 0.768/0.744 without reasoning versus 0.806/0.783 with reasoning; Table A.2 reports 0.802/0.768 for two-dataset RACT versus 0.789/0.754 for Q-Insight. Table 2 adds LIQE at 0.761/0.766, removes NIMA, and changes displayed CLIP-IQA+/ManIQA entries without explaining a setting change; CLIP-IQA+'s average SRCC changes from 0.720 to 0.658. RALI's headline 0.798/0.779 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)-(3) for clustering and scoring are unchanged. The new appendices add empirical evidence and conceptual discussion, not formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims that compact reasoning-text representations explain generalization, RACT enables cross-domain training, and RALI achieves comparable accuracy with much lower inference costs. Specifying 'during inference' in the abstract clarifies the existing claim.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explains reasoning-free training as relying on score-only constraints and discusses insufficient reasoning length. Expanded Appendix C argues that RACT benefits more from additional training domains and is insensitive to choosing KonIQ or SPAQ as the score source. Existing limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link. Appendix C newly identifies KonIQ scores and KonIQ-trained Q-Insight as the choices behind the existing Table 3 experiment. Previously documented hyperparameters, hardware and prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Jin et al. (2024) on reasoning length and Zhang et al. (2023) for LIQE, and expands discussion connecting its reasoning argument to Q-Insight and Visual-RFT. The broader related-work coverage and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 trims introductory prose, changes many instances of 'quality descriptions' to 'quality reasoning text,' adds a conference header, and inserts a new Appendix A while expanding the RACT appendix. The main section order and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three experimental appendix tables, renumbers the previous appendix tables as A.4-A.6, and relocates existing displays. Table 2's baseline rows and highlighting are revised, and several captions are clarified. The principal figures and overall layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The new no-reasoning control provides more direct support for the central explanation, while the RACT sensitivity checks and code-access information add useful evidence and documentation. Reporting problems limit the gain: Table 2's revised CLIP-IQA+ SRCC contradicts the unchanged Section 5.2 margin, and Table A.3 inconsistently averages its rows. Nevertheless, the reasoning control and individual-dataset RACT results remain informative, supporting a limited net improvement.
